key_insight: An AI-augmented digital twin that combines a mechanistic reaction–diffusion model, residual correction, and online updating can better predict brain tumor evolution and optimize treatment timing.
engineering_relevance: This framework links physics-based modeling with machine learning and model predictive control, offering a patient-specific decision-support pipeline for adaptive oncology planning.
method: Reaction–diffusion baseline models tumor growth and spatial spread.
3D residual network corrects model-form errors in long-horizon prediction.
Digital twin updates recursively and MPC schedules constrained chemo/radiotherapy.
evidence_signal: On 387 synthetic tumor trajectories over 120 time steps, the hybrid model cut masked voxel-wise MSE by 84.3% and raised Dice overlap by 43.5%, while online updating further improved MSE by 45.9% and Dice by 9.6% versus the non-updated hybrid.
watch_item: Results were validated on patient-data-informed synthetic trajectories rather than real longitudinal clinical data, so clinical robustness and deployment behavior remain unproven.
paper_title: AI-Augmented Adaptive Digital Twin Modeling for Brain Tumor Evolution Prediction and Treatment Scheduling
